items.reviewNote: Un assemblage de fous names a collection of people, rather than a manufactured joint or a process of joining. No global or earlier French assemblage family exists. Assemblage/voyage/discours/silence are masculine singular and fit un; the collection rather than movement, speech or absence of sound selects assemblage.

Both fous uses name people, including combatants judged irrational, rather than directly describing a following noun. The global fou family is an adjective only; it cannot silently own this noun. Prepare a proper French noun lemma and irrational-person meaning, preserving adjective mastery. Fous/sages/justes/savants are masculine plural substantive nouns; lack of reason selects fous.

items.meaning: wicked people; people who wish to harm
items.reviewNote: De méchants names wicked people in the assemblage, not poor-quality objects. The global méchant adjective family teaches quality and has no proper noun lemma. Prepare a French noun meaning for harmful people, preserving those adjective identities. All four substantive choices are masculine plural; intended harm rather than justice, innocence or wisdom selects méchants.

items.meaning: unfortunate people; people worthy of pity
items.reviewNote: The assemblage’s malheureux and the giant’s vocative Ah malheureux name unfortunate people. The exact published bank is adjectival, with singular adjective alternatives; this noun requires proper French nominal ownership and four masculine plural nouns. The source’s judgment is attributed to speakers, not a claim that all humans are invariably unhappy.

items.meaning: an optional expletive marker; no negation
items.reviewNote: Plus de matière qu’il ne nous en faut and plus de choses possibles qu’on ne pense contain expletive ne: the amount needed and the thinking remain affirmative. The earlier VI expletive n’ after fear bank was read. Share that planned nonnegative particle sense under the existing ne adverb lemma, broadening the licensed-context wording before import; no comparison-only sense is invented. Middle alternatives are grammatical names of particles/pronouns, distinguished by nonnegation.

items.meaning: for; towards the object of an emotion
items.reviewNote: Pitié pour names the target of compassion, rather than a purpose or exchange. The proper global pour family and the earlier viewpoint and scale-relation proposals were compared. Prepare this object-of-emotion contextual relation under the same preposition lemma; final whole-work reconciliation must compare its closeness to the broad for/beneficiary meaning before creating any fresh identity. All prepositions fit eux; directed compassion selects pour.

Tuer pour de l’argent describes payment as the motive or return for an action, rather than the bénéficiaire of killing. Prepare exchange/remuneration under the existing French pour lemma, preserving purpose and relational-analogy meanings. The source assumes the sages do not kill for payment; the bank does not accuse them of doing so. All four prepositional alternatives fit de l’argent, with payment selecting pour.

Prendre pour des sorciers assigns a mistaken classification, not a benefit or goal. The published for/purpose, earlier viewpoint and analogy senses were compared; prepare predicative taken-as under the proper existing pour lemma. Each preposition can introduce a complement after prenait, but the classification clue selects pour. This remains the dwarf’s temptation, not a supernatural claim.

items.meaning: only to; leading to a contrasting result
items.reviewNote: Pour être si ignorante contrasts alleged prenatal knowledge with later ignorance. The giant frames an ironic outcome, rather than a sincere intention to become ignorant. Prepare this resulting-state context under the existing pour lemma and reconcile goal/result overlap across the complete work before import. Alternatives are full infinitive prefixes and all attach to être; the resulting contrast selects pour.

Faire un beau livre produces a material written work, matching the global create/produce sense rather than merely doing an activity or causative faire plus infinitive. Add a contextual faire bank on that existing sense. The source promise is not proof that the later blank volume contains actual doctrine; each infinitive fits ce livre.

All three mal uses are nouns: doing harm and the supposed origin of evil in matter or mind. The global mal families are adjective and adverb only; badly does not own this noun. Prepare a proper French noun lemma and broad harm/evil meaning, without asserting the truth of either philosophical hypothesis. Mal/bien/plaisir/repos are masculine singular substantive nouns.

items.meaning: comes from; has its origin in
items.reviewNote: Both vient de la matière and vient de l’esprit ask the abstract source of harm. The existing origin sense and three light/wind-origin banks were inspected. Add this abstract-origin context; before activation impact-review wording currently limited to a direction/place and broaden transparent origin scope while preserving unchanged origin mastery. All four verbs fit en, and the source-of-origin rather than departure or escape clue selects vient.

Par toute la terre locates the practice throughout Earth. The published broad par sense explicitly includes passage and distribution, while its current bank is agent-only. Add geographical-distribution questions on that same preposition sense, preserving agent/means mastery and avoiding a location-only duplicate. All alternatives form grammatical prepositional complements; distribution selects par.

The two couverts uses describe head coverings: hats and a turban. The existing generic covering sense and earlier conditional couvrirait plan were compared; physical covering fits rather than coating a surface or concealing a fault. All four participles fit en sont and agree masculine plural. Retain the earlier shared-definition gloss-normalization dependency before activation.

items.meaning: hats; head coverings with a crown and brim
items.reviewNote: Chapeaux names hats worn by one side in the warfare contrast, without identifying an exact uniform or nationality. No proper global or earlier chapeau lemma exists. Chapeaux/casques/turbans/bonnets are masculine plural and fit des; the conventional crown-and-brim description selects hats rather than protective helmets, wound cloth or soft brimless caps.

Tuent states that the combatants kill one another’s opposing group. No global or earlier tuer lemma exists. Each plural predicate fits les; actual death rather than injury, rescue or frightening selects tuent. The source’s round numbers are kept as narrative claims rather than independently verified history.

items.meaning: turban; cloth wound around the head
items.reviewNote: Turban names the head covering of the opposing combatants, rather than a personal name or a claim about every Muslim person. No earlier or global French turban lemma exists. Turban/chapeau/casque/bonnet are masculine singular and fit un; wound fabric selects turban without a grammatical eliminator.

Sont massacrés par eux forms a passive with an explicit agent. The exact sont candidate is copular; the global proper être family has a passive auxiliary sense. Add this plural surface bank to that existing sense, while massacrés carries the lexical violent killing. Middle options are grammatical labels in the quoted auxiliary prompt; the requested être auxiliary distinguishes sont.

The alternate side is brutally killed, matching the existing massacrer violent-killing meaning. Add the masculine plural participial surface and its three banks under the proper verb lemma, not a participle-only new sense. Each alternative agrees with ils and fits ont été; the death clue selects massacrés.

Coin de terre denotes a patch of land rather than Earth as a planet or wet soil. Share the earlier III land meaning, with a new bank because its arrival-after-sea middle question could also admit montagne. The corrected clue explicitly asks for the general firm-ground name rather than a particular relief. Terre/mer/lune/montagne are feminine singular; reconcile the earlier ambiguous bank before whole-work import.

The giant shudders at the reported warfare. No French global or earlier frémir family exists. The bank tests an emotional trembling reaction, not approval of the violence; all four singular past-historic predicates are grammatical, with trembling distinct from laughter, yawning and sleep.

Quel pouvait être le sujet asks what the disputed matter could possibly be, not a person’s physical capacity. The proper pouvoir family and VI pussent target were read. Share that broad capacity/possibility meaning under sns_zola_pouvoir_present_ability, whose definition is not tense-limited; imperfect inflection does not create a fresh meaning. The exact legacy pouvait bank tests physical capacity and owns a redundant past-only sense, requiring family impact review and mastery-preserving reconciliation before import. All four predicates fit être; epistemic possibility selects pouvait.

Querelles entre de si chétifs animaux relates the participants in a reciprocal dispute rather than spatial position. The published entre definition explicitly includes relationships, and its spatial three-band bank was read. Add a reciprocal-relation context bank on that same French preposition sense, without a dispute-only meaning. All four prepositions take elles and form grammatical complements; reciprocal participation rather than opposition to an external group, absence or spatial presence selects entre.

Le sujet de ces querelles is the disputed matter, identified next as ownership of a patch of land. No earlier or global sujet family exists. Sujet/bruit/prix/poids are masculine singular after le; a general theme or matter differs from noise, a price or weight. Do not infer a grammatical subject or political subordinate.

Horribles qualifies the violent disputes as causing horror. The proper published horrible adjective sense applies; add this plural surface without a plural-only meaning. Each adjective agrees with feminine plural querelles and the source judgment is attributed to the giant.

Querelles names the disputes leading to slaughter, rather than limiting the scale to a domestic verbal squabble. No global or earlier querelle family exists. Querelles/ententes/fêtes/trêves are feminine plural, fitting des; disagreement rather than accord, celebration or suspension of conflict selects querelles.

items.meaning: puny; frail and of little strength
items.reviewNote: Chétifs expresses the giant’s perception of tiny weak animals. No global or earlier chétif adjective family exists. The bank distinguishes puniness from robustness, power and vigor with four masculine plural predicates, without asserting a scientific measurement of human strength or a moral inferiority.

items.meaning: mud; used contemptuously for the land
items.reviewNote: The two tas de boue uses disparage the land fought over by calling it mud. This is the published mud meaning used as an image; no assertion that the actual region is wet and no territory-only new sense is made. The global definition and literal three-band bank were inspected. The new contextual bank explains the image; boue/neige/glace/poussière are feminine singular after la.

Ce n’est pas qu’aucun… prétende denies that any of the combatants claims even a straw of the disputed land. Aucun is literary any, not a second negative meaning none; otherwise the logic reverses. Académie records positive literary use in negative-colored clauses. The earlier II aucuns_none_pronoun plan and three bands were read: reuse its planned pronoun lemma with a distinct positive-any meaning. Before import, repair that earlier plan’s incorrect determiner lemma target to a proper pronoun owner, retaining the unchanged negative meaning and mastery. The middle labels distinguish any from every, specified and all.

Presque aucun de ces animaux n’a jamais vu the ruler means almost none, under negative n’a. This independent pronoun with a de complement shares the earlier II aucuns_none_pronoun negative meaning; singular versus historical plural creates a surface, not a meaning. All three earlier questions were read. Repair the earlier plan’s determiner lemma target to the proper shared pronoun owner before import, without changing its meaning or mastery. This bank shares that meaning; the positive-any bank adds a distinct meaning on the same owner. The metalinguistic alternatives remain grammatical.

items.meaning: have something done; cause an action
items.reviewNote: Se font égorger is a pronominal causative with the combatants as patients; en font remercier Dieu makes others offer thanks. The existing faire causative sense and three infinitive-causation banks were inspected, contrasting activity, forming an idea and making into a state. Add font on the same proper verb sense. Se does not imply the combatants voluntarily choose death, and no simple do meaning is approved for these two infinitive constructions.

Tout était fait uniquement pour l’homme claims the universe was made for humankind as a whole, rather than a single adult man. The existing proper homme noun definition includes human being, while its three questions test individual male adults. Add a generic-humankind contextual bank to that same broad meaning, with final family wording review before import and no generic-number-only new sense. Homme/ours/aigle/éléphant are masculine singular nouns beginning with a vowel after l’; the explicit human-species clue selects homme. The cleric’s cosmological claim is attributed to him, not asserted as fact.

Se font égorger refers to slaughter in warfare, not proof that every soldier’s throat is literally cut. No earlier or global égorger family exists; prepare this figurative violent-killing meaning under a proper French verb lemma. All four infinitives fit les, contrasting killing with protection, rescue and sparing. The later égorgent forms share this same meaning.

Un fétu is an insignificant straw, illustrating that the fighters claim not even the smallest thing on the land. No global or earlier fétu family exists. Fétu/trésor/royaume/palais are masculine singular after un, with the straw image rather than great value, territory or a building selecting fétu. The bank does not assert a literal straw was demanded.

items.meaning: will belong to; will be the property of
items.reviewNote: Appartiendra asks whether the disputed territory will be the property of one ruler or the other, not membership in a group. The global property sense and earlier appartenir whale-ownership bank were read. Add the future surface on that existing sense, preserving the group-membership meaning; all four verbs take lui in the unchanged construction.

items.meaning: sultan; a title of a Muslim sovereign
items.reviewNote: Sultan is a ruler’s title, contrasted with César, rather than a particular personal name. Académie records the Ottoman and other Muslim sovereign title. No French published or earlier sultan lemma exists. Sultan/empereur/président/duc are masculine singular labels in the unchanged prompt; the conventional title selects sultan. Source capitalization does not create a case-only meaning.

Le petit coin de terre is a small area of land, not a wedge or the meeting of two walls. The global coin noun family has wedge and geometric/spatial-corner banks but no general small-place meaning. Prepare that contextual place sense under the existing noun lemma, comparing possible scope overlap before import. Coin/angle/centre/plafond are masculine singular; the explicit no-angle small-place clue selects coin.

Both s’égorgent uses describe reciprocal slaughter among the combatants, the same figurative violent-killing meaning as égorger above. Reuse that planned French verb meaning with a new inflected bank, not a literal-throat-only or tense-only sense. All alternatives begin with vowels after the unchanged s’ and form grammatical plural pronominal predicates; slaughter differs from helping, encouragement and avoidance.

Mutuellement marks reciprocal killing, not merely simultaneous or sequential activity. No global or earlier French mutuellement family exists. The four adverbs are grammatical labels; reciprocal direction rather than timing, succession or separation selects mutuellement, without endorsing the violent act described.
